subject: Urgent: sustained p95 drift — decision needed on protective routing vs. token-throttles
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observed sustained p95 drift across us-west checkout traffic

Team —

Alerting caught a sustained p95 uplift across checkout paths starting ~07:45 PST and persisting; looks concentrated on the tokenized cart route (gen-api/v1/complete) with increased tail latency on sequences >512. Attached CSV has p50/p95/p99 deltas by host.

What I see so far:
- p95 moved from ~220ms to 520-700ms for a subset of hosts
- throughput held steady but there are intermittent queue spikes on a few instances
- KV-cache hitrate dropped ~8% (see qos_trace) — possible eviction noise after a deploy?

Immediate asks:
1) SRE: Can you confirm infra-level signal (instance CPU/GPU stalls, network) vs. runtime (KV thrash, tokenization)?
2) Eng: If runtime, do we have a hotpath candidate to revert or a targeted config (quantization shim) to roll back?
3) Product/CS: I can prep a short customer note for Checkoutly if we intend a temporary protective measure (routing or throttles).

I created SRV-9123 and attached a short proposal for protective routing as a 15-min mitigation. Posting traces and CSV now.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed sustained p95 drift across us-west checkout traffic

On Wed, Jul 28, 2027 at 8:15 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Alerting caught a sustained p95 uplift...

Thanks Soojin — I've pulled runtime traces. Early signal points to a KV-cache eviction storm on a small subset of model shards after the deploy (2027.07.27-runtime). The runtime shows repeated cache warmups and elevated attention-kernel latencies for seq>512.

Immediate engineering options (short list):
- Roll back the runtime deploy on impacted shard group (fast, higher blast radius)
- Apply protective routing: route Checkoutly traffic to a warmed pool (safer, needs routing rule and capacity pin)
- Soft token-throttle: enforce a per-route cap for sequences >512 for Checkoutly (low change surface, may impact customer UX for long requests)

I recommend Protective routing as the least risky immediate mitigation while we evaluate root cause. If we do protective routing, we should also schedule a short maintenance window to roll back the runtime deploy if metrics don't improve.

I'll stand by on SRV-9123 for logs/trace correlation.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed sustained p95 drift across us-west checkout traffic

+1 on protective routing for timeboxed mitigation. From product POV:
- We need a clear customer comms plan (one short advisory + follow-up postmortem)
- If protective routing adds ~5-10% cost (warmer pool), we need an approval path to grant temporary credits if Checkoutly requests mercy for cost delta

Ben — can you draft the advisory? Keep it candid and include expected timeline and mitigation. Also: get Ops/CS on a quick sync with Checkoutly to explain the UX tradeoffs for token-throttle vs. routing.

Attachment: protective-routing-proposal-v1.pdf (short runbook + rollback steps).

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Product — Serving & Ops
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Garth Flynn <garth@checkoutly.com>, ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: (Customer) Brief advisory: degraded tail latency on certain long requests — targeted mitigation

Garth / Checkoutly ops —

Wanted to flag that our monitoring shows elevated tail latency for long sequences on your checkout generator route. We're actively investigating and have a temporary mitigation we can enable which will route your long-sequence requests to a warmed capacity pool while we complete root-cause analysis.

What to expect if we enable the mitigation:
- Short-term: improved tail latency for long requests, minor chance of throttling for extremely long sequences if queueing occurs
- Cost: routing to warmed capacity may increase cost ~5–8% while active; we can discuss credits if this runs beyond the next 24–48 hours
- Action: we can enable the routing now and monitor impact for 1–2 hours; rollback if not improved

Please reply with approval to enable or let us know if you prefer we try a token-throttle pilot instead (that may reduce throughput of very long requests).

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Garth Flynn <garth@checkoutly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: (Customer) Brief advisory: degraded tail latency on certain long requests — targeted mitigation

Ben — thanks for the heads up. Please enable the routing mitigation now. We prefer routing vs throttles as throttles would break a small number of flows. We'll take cost credits if that makes sense. Please keep us updated in the hour.

— Garth Flynn
VP Product, Checkoutly
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation note and next steps

Folks —

Quick update after routing was enabled per Checkoutly approval:
- p95 for Checkoutly long requests improved from ~640ms -> ~230ms within 18 minutes of rule application (see attached p95_delta CSV).
- No observable throughput loss; warmed pool cost delta tracked at ~6.2% across the 12-hour window.
- KV-cache eviction spikes subsided but traces show residual attention kernel variance tied to the recent runtime change.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Karthik / Eng: Prepare a narrow rollback candidate for the runtime deploy targeting impacted shards; plan to test in staging and schedule a controlled rollback window (SL: 48 hours)
2) SRE: Keep SRV-9123 open and annotate runbook with the mitigation timeline and metrics captured
3) Product/CS (Marissa / Ben): Draft a brief postmortem for Checkoutly and confirm any cost credit we commit (suggest 25% of delta for up to 48 hours)

I'll own the customer PM/ops coordination. If we don't have a rollback candidate in 48h, we'll schedule a full cross-functional review to decide on longer-term mitigations (quantization thresholds vs. cache tuning vs. routing policy changes).

— Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
